claim: Changing the identity source of IAM Identity Center might remove all user and group assignments; if that happens, all users, including the administrative user, lose single sign-on access to their AWS accounts and applications.
question: What can happen to assignments and access when the IAM Identity Center identity source is changed?

values.display: might remove all user and group assignments
will lose single sign-on access

qualifiers.condition: users and groups already managed in one identity source

evidence.quote: If you are already managing users and groups in one identity source, changing to a different identity source might remove all user and group assignments that you configured in IAM Identity Center. If this occurs, all users, including the administrative user in IAM Identity Center, will lose single sign-on access to their AWS accounts and applications.

integrated applications and accounts

claim: A replicated (multi-Region) IAM Identity Center must use an external identity provider or the Identity Center directory as identity source; multi-Region support is not available for Active Directory.
question: Which identity sources can a multi-Region IAM Identity Center instance use?

values.display: Multi-Region support is not available for Active Directory
external identity provider or the Identity Center directory

qualifiers.scope: IAM Identity Center replicated to additional Regions

evidence.quote: If you have replicated IAM Identity Center to additional Regions or plan to do so, you must use an external identity provider or the Identity Center directory as the identity source. Multi-Region support is not available for Active Directory.

claim: IAM Identity Center supports automatic provisioning (synchronization) of user and group information from an external IdP into IAM Identity Center with the SCIM v2.0 protocol, configured in the IdP with the IAM Identity Center SCIM endpoint and a bearer token.
question: How are users and groups from an external IdP such as Okta created in IAM Identity Center automatically?

values.display: automatic provisioning (synchronization) of user and group information
a bearer token that you create

qualifiers.scope: external identity provider as identity source

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center supports automatic provisioning (synchronization) of user and group information from your identity provider (IdP) into IAM Identity Center using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) v2.0 protocol.
You configure this connection in your IdP using your SCIM endpoint for IAM Identity Center and a bearer token that you create in IAM Identity Center.

claim: With SCIM, the identity provider controls provisioning and update intervals; changes to users and groups in the IdP appear in IAM Identity Center only after the IdP sends them.
question: When do user and group changes in an external IdP appear in IAM Identity Center?

values.display: controlled by your identity provider
only reflected in IAM Identity Center after

qualifiers.scope: SCIM provisioning from an external identity provider

evidence.quote: SCIM provisioning and update intervals are controlled by your identity provider. Changes to users and groups in your identity provider are only reflected in IAM Identity Center after your identity provider sends those changes to IAM Identity Center.

claim: With an external SAML 2.0 IdP, the assertion's Subject NameID must exactly match the Username of a user provisioned in IAM Identity Center; sign-in fails without a match even when the IdP authenticated the user.
question: Can a user from an external SAML IdP sign in to IAM Identity Center without being provisioned there?

values.display: must exactly match the **Username**
Sign-in fails

evidence.quote: The SAML assertion's `Subject` `NameID` value must exactly match the **Username** of a user provisioned in IAM Identity Center. Sign-in fails if IAM Identity Center cannot match the `NameID` to a **Username**, even when the external IdP authenticates the user successfully.

note: d057: users must exist (SCIM or manual provisioning) before SAML sign-in works

claim: With Active Directory as the identity source, IAM Identity Center uses the Directory Service connection for pass-through authentication to the source AD; it synchronizes users, groups and memberships, but no password information, because authentication happens in the source directory.
question: Does IAM Identity Center copy Active Directory passwords when AD is the identity source?

values.display: pass-through authentication to the source AD instance
No password information is synchronized to IAM Identity Center

qualifiers.scope: Active Directory as the IAM Identity Center identity source

evidence.quote: IAM Identity Center uses the connection provided by Directory Service to perform pass-through authentication to the source AD instance.
No password information is synchronized to IAM Identity Center, because user authentication takes place directly from the source directory in Active Directory.

claim: To use Active Directory as the identity source, an AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory in AWS Directory Service must reside in the AWS Organizations management account, or in the IAM Identity Center delegated administrator account when delegated admin is used.
question: In which account must the AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory be for IAM Identity Center to use it?

values.display: must reside within your AWS Organizations management account
residing in the delegated admin account

qualifiers.scope: Active Directory as the IAM Identity Center identity source

evidence.quote: You must have an existing AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory set up in AWS Directory Service, and it must reside within your AWS Organizations management account.

If you plan to enable IAM Identity Center delegated admin and use Active Directory as your IAM Identity Center identity source, you can use an existing AD Connector or AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory set up in AWS Directory residing in the delegated admin account.

claim: IAM Identity Center can connect only one AD Connector directory or one AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory at a time; to support multiple domains or forests, AWS says to use AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
question: How many directories can IAM Identity Center connect at once, and which directory type supports multiple domains or forests?

values.display: connect only one AD Connector directory
support multiple domains or forests

qualifiers.scope: Active Directory as the IAM Identity Center identity source

evidence.quote: You can connect only one AD Connector directory or one directory in AWS Managed Microsoft AD at a time. If you need to support multiple domains or forests, use AWS Managed Microsoft AD.

claim: With AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source, IAM Identity Center must be enabled in the same AWS Region as the directory, and the AWS access portal uses the directory's access URL.
question: In which Region must IAM Identity Center run when AWS Managed Microsoft AD is its identity source?

values.display: in the same AWS Region
uses the same access URL as your directory

qualifiers.scope: AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the identity source

evidence.quote: If you are using AWS Managed Microsoft AD, you must enable IAM Identity Center in the same AWS Region where your AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory is set up.
Also, note that the AWS access portal uses the same access URL as your directory.

claim: IAM Identity Center can connect a self-managed Active Directory or an AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory through AWS Directory Service; with AWS Managed Microsoft AD as the source it can work with users from any domain connected through an AD trust.
question: How can IAM Identity Center use users from an on-premises Active Directory?

values.display: connect a self-managed directory in Active Directory
any domain connected through an AD trust

qualifiers.scope: Active Directory as the IAM Identity Center identity source

evidence.quote: With AWS IAM Identity Center, you can connect a self-managed directory in Active Directory (AD) or a directory in AWS Managed Microsoft AD by using AWS Directory Service.
When you use AWS Managed Microsoft AD as your identity source, IAM Identity Center can work with users from AWS Managed Microsoft AD or from any domain connected through an AD trust.
